_notes: One fix per live parish problem (generation/parishes.ts). weeks at apPerWeek from the routine; cost drawn weekly from parish cash. A vicar may begin only with the pastor's leave (relationship). On completion the parish problem becomes 'none' and the effects apply; fixed:<problem> is flagged.

fixes.label: Broaden the base
fixes.blurb: A stewardship drive, a hundred small pledges, and a dinner where the big family is thanked and quietly outnumbered.
fixes.outcome: The pledge cards come back. The family still gives, and still knows it, but the collection no longer holds its breath when they travel.

fixes.label: Take the office back
fixes.blurb: New job descriptions, a calendar the pastor keeps, and one retirement party nobody enjoys.
fixes.outcome: The office runs on your schedule now. One of the staff left and two stayed, and the ones who stayed are better than you thought.

fixes.label: Settle the music
fixes.blurb: A meeting with the director, a meeting with the choir, and a decision about what the parish sings that you will have to stand behind.
fixes.outcome: The choir sings what you decided it would sing. Some of them quit. The Mass is quieter and the arguments have moved to the parking lot, which is where they belong.

fixes.label: Rework the school's money
fixes.blurb: A tuition-assistance fund, a sponsor-a-student drive, and a hard look at the budget with the principal.
fixes.outcome: Enrollment steadies. Twenty families who were going to leave stay, and the school's deficit is a number you can say out loud at council.

fixes.label: Prepare the handover
fixes.blurb: The files in order, the council briefed, the old man given a retirement he can accept and a Mass in his honor.
fixes.outcome: The parish knows what happens next, which is most of what it wanted. The old pastor cries at his own Mass and pretends not to.

fixes.label: Replace the roof
fixes.blurb: Bids, a diocesan loan or a campaign, scaffolding through Lent.
fixes.outcome: The buckets go back to the basement. The church is dry for the first time in a decade, and the people notice the ceiling again.

fixes.label: Make the case to the chancery
fixes.blurb: Numbers, a plan, the council in a room with the vicar general, and a parish that shows up when it is asked to.
fixes.outcome: The parish comes off the list, or at least the list stops being mentioned. You have made a promise to the chancery about the numbers that you will have to keep.

fixes.label: Replace the boiler
fixes.blurb: Before the winter, if the bids come back in time; after it, if they do not.
fixes.outcome: Heat, on the first cold Sunday. The old boiler goes out on a flatbed and a few of the men stand and watch it like a funeral.

fixes.label: Give the convent a use
fixes.blurb: A lease to a ministry, a shelter, a retreat house, or a sale the sisters can bear.
fixes.outcome: The convent has lights on at night again. The two sisters approve of the use, mostly, and the parish stops paying to heat forty empty rooms.

fixes.label: Meet the new neighborhood
fixes.blurb: A census of the blocks, a Mass in the language that is spoken now, and a welcome the old guard will resent.
fixes.outcome: New faces at the ten o'clock, then at the noon. The parish is becoming what the neighborhood is. Some of the founders stop coming, and some of them come back.

fixes.label: Cut the Mass schedule
fixes.blurb: Seven Masses to five, announced in Advent, argued about until Easter.
fixes.outcome: Five Masses, fuller. The 7:30 crowd has not forgiven you and never will. The priests sleep.

fixes.label: Make the parish a safe place
fixes.blurb: A know-your-rights night, a word with the police chief, rides for the families who stopped driving.
fixes.outcome: The parking lot fills again, slowly. You have made friends and enemies in town you did not have before.

fixes.label: Build or borrow a hall
fixes.blurb: An addition, or a deal with the school gym, or a tent for the feast day and a plan for the rest.
fixes.outcome: The hall holds the parish, or near enough. The groups stop fighting over Tuesday nights.

fixes.label: Honor the founders
fixes.blurb: A history night, their names on a plaque, a seat for them on every committee that matters and a clear word about who else sits there.
fixes.outcome: The old guard has a plaque and a place, and stops writing to the bishop. The parish belongs to everyone in it, which the founders admit only in private.

fixes.label: Clear the backlog
fixes.blurb: Group baptisms, a quinceañera Mass a month, lay catechists trained and trusted.
fixes.outcome: The wait drops to a season. The catechists run the classes and you sign the certificates, which is what a pastor is for.

fixes.label: Make one parish of three
fixes.blurb: A shared council, a shared bulletin, a rotation of Masses that no church likes and every church accepts.
fixes.outcome: Three churches that argue like a family instead of like strangers. The rotation holds. Your truck knows the roads.

fixes.label: Build a bench
fixes.blurb: A deacon formed, a retired priest coaxed, a supply arrangement with the diocese for the weeks you are down.
fixes.outcome: There is someone to call. The old priest an hour away is grateful, and so are you, in a way you did not expect.

fixes.label: Carry the farms through
fixes.blurb: A hardship fund, the assessment negotiated, a word with the bank that owns half the county.
fixes.outcome: Nobody lost the farm this year because of the church. The collection comes back with the rain.

fixes.label: Settle the cemetery
fixes.blurb: A board, a rule book, a perpetual-care fund, and the argument about the fence ended by decree.
fixes.outcome: The cemetery has rules and a fund and a board that meets twice a year. The argument about the fence has become an argument about the sign, which is progress.

fixes.label: Give the young a reason
fixes.blurb: A young-adult night that is not a lecture, a connection to the city parish they will land in, and a wedding policy that brings them home.
fixes.outcome: Some come back for more than funerals. A few stay. The parish looks, on a good Sunday, like it has a future.

fixes.label: Say what happened
fixes.blurb: A listening session, a letter that says the true thing in the plainest words the chancery will allow, and a Mass of healing.
fixes.outcome: The cloud has a shape now. Some people needed to hear it said; some needed never to hear it again. The parish breathes.

fixes.label: Stitch the parish back
fixes.blurb: The two camps at one table, a council with both on it, and a year of preaching that never once mentions the last pastor.
fixes.outcome: They still sit on opposite sides, but they sit in the same church and serve on the same council. The last pastor is not mentioned.

fixes.label: See the lawsuit through
fixes.blurb: The diocesan lawyers, the insurers, the depositions, and a settlement or a verdict the parish can survive.
fixes.outcome: It is over. The number is in the paper for one day. The parish paid, and you were the one who kept showing up.

fixes.label: Clean up after the theft
fixes.blurb: An audit, the police, new controls, and the humiliation of asking the parish to trust the office again.
fixes.outcome: Two signatures on every check. The audit is clean. The bookkeeper is gone and the parish knows why, which it needed to.

fixes.label: Make a place for the Latin Mass
fixes.blurb: A settled time, a settled chapel, a chaplain named, and a limit spoken aloud that both sides hear.
fixes.outcome: The community has its Mass and its hour and its chaplain, and the parish has the rest of the schedule. Neither side is satisfied, which means it is settled.
